requirements.summary: The console decision should preserve the topic-intelligence plane and its nine named views for deciding what to monitor and whether a problem remains worth pursuing.
The console decision should preserve the campaign plane and its five named views for explaining each round and why work stopped.
The console decision should preserve the verification-and-release plane and its proof, provenance, novelty, decision, and disclosure views.
The visual baseline must preserve the three blueprint token modes: root, system dark, and explicit dark, together with the declared component classes.
The console shell must preserve the top bar, plane switcher, and three-column application structure declared by the blueprint.
Every console view must carry exactly one of the blueprint's five construction states, and an implemented state must be backed by automated evidence.
M0 must export an audited workspace to a versioned console.json outside the workspace, clear stale snapshots on fetch failure, and visibly disclose demo fallback data.
The live observer must stream research_event records over SSE with an ordered cursor that supports continuation.
M1 must use read-only observer GET endpoints and SSE, keep campaign reports bound to the current workspace, and coalesce an event into one dashboard refresh.
M2 must expose the review queue and review bundle as reads, accept roster-token review submission only at POST /api/review, and reject every other write route.
Review approval must require every obligation verdict to be OK; records must be revision-bound and become SUPERSEDED on mismatch, while can_review remains object-specific.
The console must read the real roster and review queue, render the bundle and obligation decisions, submit through the unique review endpoint, and keep the token in memory only.
M3 must project SourceRegistry, SourceObservation, LiteratureBase, the single-topic cursor, and the human queue read-only, without authorizing a data-entry surface.
The console must render fixed-source R1 records for all four named retrieval routes, including each case's scope, hits, and unresolved items.
The console must render the three T2 archive contracts with case identity, expected state, human rationale, and non-promotion boundary while leaving execution and recovery to the backend runner.
M4 must provide the account overview, credit ledger, recharge-and-plan, and budget-and-limit surfaces declared by the blueprint.
The operations ledger must remain local and isolated from the research core; identity, payment, and real upstream routing require separate approval and integration.

Account and administration views must read independent local credit, seat, billing, and upstream ledgers outside the research workspace and show external identity, payment, and upstream connections as not_configured.
The browser acceptance matrix must render all 52 blueprint-defined view/state cases for both campaigns with no page error or undefined, NaN, or object-string leakage.
At each of the six desktop widths from 1240 through 1920, every paired column must satisfy the declared natural-height difference and ratio thresholds.
The five ledger-tamper modes must produce the blueprint's distinct validation outcomes, including external-head rejection for a fully rewritten chain.
Release must fail if the console invents numbers: counts must be derived, protocol parameters must cite a source version, and pseudo-precise difficulty scores are forbidden.
Release must preserve honest empty states: an empty campaign cannot borrow data and a rejected promotion cannot create or visually fabricate an event.
Human release review must reject any capability claim without its four-state chip or any presentation of planned capability as implemented behavior.
